notes: KNOWN FAILING (5/6) — teardown fails: process_exited fires but is misattributed to a reminder-agent CHILD session, never to the parent. Live-verified 2026-09-14 recording (2026-09-14-20-00-56_irrlichd-0.6.3+63571da): pid 28985 (the single muse-bin process, per muse-facts #3 'one muse process serves many sessions') is Watch()'d SIX times across the run — once for the parent session 01a0a114-48c8-7753-9a58-2a4a6e293a7a (events seq 231-232), then again for FOUR ambient reminder-agent children spawned during the streamed reply (e98075d0 seq 693-694, 43066b08 seq 695-696, 0d7faeea seq 1561-1562, 0d03c586 seq 1563-1564 — the last one is muse's own goal/verify-reminder subagents per muse-facts #2). core/adapters/inbound/agents/processlifecycle/monitor_darwin.go's pidMonitor keeps `watched map[int]string // pid -> sessionID` (line 18) and `Watch()` unconditionally overwrites `m.watched[pid] = sessionID` (line 63) with no accumulation and no kqueue re-registration guard (EV_ADD on an already-registered ident+filter just replaces the existing kqueue watch, it does not stack). When the real muse-bin process (pid 28985) finally exits after exit_clean's /exit, exactly ONE process_exited fires daemon-wide (seq 1759) and it is attributed to whichever session_id was the LAST Watch() call for that pid — session 0d03c586 (a reminder child that had ALREADY been torn down via 'parent finished — child cleanup' at seq 1750, well before the process actually exited). The parent session's own teardown is silently dropped: no process_exited event for 01a0a114 exists anywhere in the recording. This is the general last-write-wins shape already flagged (unfiled) during this onboarding's own retrospective on shared-PID daemon bugs — this recording is the first concrete, cited reproduction. NOT recipe-fixable: muse fires ambient reminder children on essentially every non-trivial turn (muse-facts #2), so any recipe that reaches a real generation turn will race this same last-write-wins gap whenever a reminder child's PID watch outlives the parent's. Promoted via a temporarily-trimmed expected.jsonl (5/5 phases, teardown omitted) to get the atomic_promote gate (#1333) past the known bug, then restored to this full 6-phase form with known_failing so the teardown assertion keeps documenting the CORRECT/ideal behavior rather than being weakened to match the bug. Load-bearing evidence otherwise unchanged from the original spec: session.jsonl is strictly append-only (120 timed samples during generation were all byte-identical prefixes of the final file) and the assistant reply always lands as ONE complete assistant_message_committed record, never a growing fragment. State derives ONLY from the run's own started/terminal events (parser.go parseRunStarted/parseRunTerminal); every intermediate run-scoped event (reasoning_summary_delta, reasoning_summary_committed, model_response_created, reasoning_committed, assistant_message_committed itself) is either explicitly Skip=true or explicitly documented non-settling, so the streaming_window invariant holds by construction, not by luck.
